title: Keep the update transcript out of world-writable /tmp
head: cf919bc59a74
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Open PR #12094 merges cleanly but directs locked-out users to the old transcript path
leads.consequence: With a valid per-user runtime dir and both PRs merged, a concurrent update gets exit 1 and 'An Omarchy update is already running', but no follow command because the other PR tests /tmp/omarchy-update.log rather than the inherited OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG. If an old /tmp file remains, the printed tail command follows stale data instead of the current transcript. The next retry still sees the lock until the first run ends. Use the exported path from the updater in the lock helper, with a same-default fallback for direct invocations; update that PR's lock test, which currently only greps the script source.

leads.summary: The new analyzer early exit must not skip independently required checks from open PRs #6840 and #11023
leads.consequence: These unstacked PRs append safety actions after the old analyzer's grep: #6840's boot image verifier can block an unsafe reboot, and #11023's extra-LUKS checker warns about an unbootable configuration. If the log is removed or the analyzer runs standalone without one, preserving this PR's new exit 0 while resolving the shared hunk silently skips both. On an update where the log disappears after script starts, update status/restart and subsequent steps proceed; a later run without a log repeats the skip. Restrict the missing-file guard to log-specific greps, leaving non-log safety checks reachable. This is an integration requirement for these pending PRs, not a claim that the pinned head already contains their helpers.
leads.triage: factual; verified via gh api patches (coord-triage/pr6840-analyze.patch, pr11023-analyze.patch); Opus self-check also confirmed; only affects standalone runs

leads.summary: New regression test passes when root continues updating or the analyzer ignores an explicit log override
leads.consequence: The root assertion greps only the refusal text, and suppresses the real status; it never checks that script was not called. A regression removing the guard's exit still proceeds under root and can create a root-owned transcript. The script stub records only its last argument and never re-execs, while analyzer cases explicitly set OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG; changing the update's call to 'env -u OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG omarchy-update-analyze-logs' makes a real run with an explicit log override analyze the default path instead, but all eight assertions still pass. Add an exit-status and no-script-call assertion for fakeroot, then have a stub re-exec through script/lock and verify the analyzer sees the produced pathname (or test this separately).
leads.triage: confirmed from test source (root case only greps output, never asserts script_calls empty); merged with Opus's surviving-mutant note

leads.summary: Open PR #12835's corrected initramfs classifier conflicts with this PR's new test expectation
leads.consequence: PR #12835 intentionally treats a bare 'Updating linux initcpios' hook banner as a no-op, but this test demands an error for exactly that content. Integrating the corrected classifier while retaining this PR's test fails the shell suite before its missing-log assertion runs; leaving the old classifier keeps #12835's false warning. Amend this test to include an actual started image build without a success marker or a real FAILED marker, while retaining the no-file and success cases. This is an integration/test conflict, not evidence that #12835's intended no-op behavior is wrong.
leads.triage: factual; verified via #12835 patch and test line 75; Opus review5 run confirms

leads.summary: A supplied non-private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is accepted before any privacy validation
leads.consequence: When the caller inherits or sets XDG_RUNTIME_DIR to /tmp, or to a directory writable by other users, the updater immediately passes that directory's predictable omarchy-update.log to script(1). Other users can pre-create the file and block updates or read a newly created typescript there under an ordinary permissive umask; a later omarchy-update-stay-awake validation rejects the unsafe directory only after logging and some update work. For a nonempty runtime path, validate ownership, directory mode and parent trust before starting script, or select a verified per-user state directory (do not treat an arbitrary nonempty value as proof of privacy). Normal systemd-created 0700 runtimes are safe; this issue concerns mis-set or user-supplied environments.
leads.triage: dropped: requires the caller to point XDG_RUNTIME_DIR at a shared directory (self-misconfiguration); systemd provides a private 0700 dir

leads.summary: Three unstacked transcript PRs cannot retain the same no-runtime fallback and test expectations
leads.consequence: Open #8429 selects a state-directory fallback, #7995 selects the state directory even when a runtime dir exists, and #12109 selects a per-user cache fallback plus a different lock dir. Each conflicts textually with this PR's changes to both transcript scripts; this PR's test asserts /tmp when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is absent, and its runtime test asserts the runtime-dir root path, so adopting any of the alternate locations requires updating the test and ensuring the producer, analyzer, lock and docs agree. Do not merge the files by preserving each PR's fallback in separate scripts; that would send standalone analysis to a different file from the producer. Decide one location policy and reconcile the corresponding tests and docs as a unit.
leads.triage: factual; verified file lists via gh api; #12109 not in Opus final, added; Opus self-check corrected #8429 wording and found #12109 adds the same test path (verified)

leads.summary: The updated process document omits the retained /tmp fallback and override from the transcript path
leads.consequence: The state table promises '$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-update.log' in a per-user private dir, and the analyzer table names that as the fallback, but unset or empty XDG_RUNTIME_DIR still puts both producer and analyzer at /tmp/omarchy-update.log. Standalone troubleshooting on a headless session will look in the wrong place, and the old cross-user collision and world-readable transcript risk remains in that mode; an explicit OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG may choose another location. Update both doc rows to spell out the /tmp fallback and override, and qualify the private-path security statement.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `cf919bc` (rebased since the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12957#issuecomment-5785493049) of `5dc63e6`), a plain `sudo omarchy update` no longer reaches the new root refusal.

**Earlier review:** all verified results and the `/tmp` fallback limit still apply, except the root refusal.

### Plain `sudo` stops before the root refusal

The rebase put the `EUID` check (line 91) after `omarchy_security_require_source_root` (line 19). sudo's environment reset drops `OMARCHY_PATH`, so the run exits with `OMARCHY_PATH does not match this Omarchy command.`, not the new refusal. **Impact:** no transcript is written, but plain `sudo` gets that error instead of the clear refusal the PR describes; the `fakeroot` test keeps `OMARCHY_PATH`.

**Suggested change:** move the `EUID` block and its comment to right after `set -e`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at cf919bc)</summary>

Append this case to `test/shell.d/update-log-path-test.sh` (it reuses that file's fixture, `script` stub and `$script_calls`). `env -i` stands in for sudo's default environment reset, which drops `OMARCHY_PATH`; `fakeroot` makes the run UID 0, as the existing root case in the file already does.

```bash
# sudo resets the environment by default, so a plain `sudo omarchy update`
# arrives without OMARCHY_PATH. The root refusal should still be what it prints.
plain_sudo_out=$(env -i PATH=/usr/bin SCRIPT_CALLS="$script_calls" \
  fakeroot "$SUDO_TEST_ROOT/bin/omarchy-update" 2>&1 || true)
grep -q "not under sudo" <<<"$plain_sudo_out" ||
  fail "update refuses a plain sudo run (environment reset) as root" "$plain_sudo_out"
pass "update refuses a plain sudo run (environment reset) as root"
```

At cf919bc:

```console
$ bash test/shell.d/update-log-path-test.sh

ok - update refuses to run as root

OMARCHY_PATH does not match this Omarchy command.

```

With the `EUID` block moved to directly after `set -e` in `bin/omarchy-update` (nothing else changed):

<details><summary>More findings: the shell tests now fail when run as root</summary>

### Update tests fail as root

Five existing test files that run `omarchy-update` (`update-user-path`, `update-hook-security`, `update-disk-space`, `update-sequence`, `channel-sudo-boundary`) pass as root at the base `324f0ba` but fail at `cf919bc`. The new `update-log-path-test.sh` also fails as root. **Impact:** this matters only if the suite is run as root (for example in a root container). Some update tests already have root-specific branches (`update-lock-test.sh`, `update-stay-awake-security-test.sh`). As an ordinary user, nothing regresses.

**Suggested change:** if root runs are supported, give these tests an EUID 0 path (at least a `skip` for the new file's update cases). Otherwise, document that the shell suite runs as an ordinary user.

Run the update tests as root, here as user-namespace root (the same UID 0 a root container gives), from the repository root.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Earlier review claims at `cf919bc`:**

| Earlier claim | Status at `cf919bc` |
| --- | --- |
| Transcript path survives the `script(1)` and lock re-execs; analyzer reads it | Still holds |
| Valid private `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` keeps transcript and lock there; no `/tmp` transcript | Still holds |
| Explicit `OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG` is passed to `script` | Still holds |

**Root runs, simulated with mock sudo** (UID 0 from `fakeroot` and from user-namespace root, same results):

| Root environment | base `324f0ba` | head `cf919bc` | head, refusal after `set -e` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plain `sudo` (no `OMARCHY_PATH`) | source-root error, no `script` | same as base | clear refusal |
| `sudo -E` | reaches `script` with `/tmp/omarchy-update.log` | clear refusal, after `sudo -k` and `sudo -h` | clear refusal, no sudo calls |
| `sudo -i` | reaches `script` with `/tmp/omarchy-update.log` | clear refusal, after `sudo -k` and `sudo -h` | clear refusal, no sudo calls |

**PR description:** at the current base, a plain `sudo omarchy update` already stops at the source-root check before `script` runs, so it cannot leave a root-owned `/tmp/omarchy-update.log`. That failure mode applies to 4.0.4 and, at the base, to `sudo -E`, `sudo -i` and root shells, which the new refusal covers.

**Related open PRs:**
- #12094 adds a hint that hard-codes `tail -f /tmp/omarchy-update.log` to `omarchy-update-lock`. After this PR, that hint would point at the wrong file.
- #8429 uses the same runtime-dir path with a state-directory fallback; #7995 and #12109 move the transcript elsewhere. #12109 also adds `test/shell.d/update-log-path-test.sh`, the same path as this PR's new test. #11217 is another fix for #11204.
- #12835 stops warning on a bare `Updating linux initcpios` banner, which `update-log-path-test.sh:75` expects to warn on.
- #6840 and #11023 append checks that do not depend on the log to the end of the analyzer. The new early `exit 0` would skip those checks when no transcript exists.

**Optional notes:**
- `docs/update-process.md:26` and `:311` leave out the retained `/tmp` fallback. Writing `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-update.log` (override: `OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG`), as the lock row does, would match the code.
- The new test still passes 8/8 when the analyzer's fallback is changed to `/tmp`, or when `export OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG` and the `env` pass-through are both dropped. The root case also never checks that `script` was not called. A standalone analyzer case with only `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` set would catch the fallback change; having the `script` stub also record `$OMARCHY_UPDATE_LOG` from its environment would catch the dropped export; an empty-`$script_calls` assertion would pin the root case.
- The description's `That closes **#11204**` is not registered as a closing reference. `Closes #11204` would link the issue.
</details>
